{{nihongo|'''Morosugi Shrine'''|諸杉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tajima Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
The enshrined deity is the following one kami<ref name="説明板">Precinct information board.</ref>:
* '''Tajima-Morosuku-no-Kami''' (たじまもろすくのかみ)
*: In the '{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}},' the name is written as "Tajima-Morosuku," and in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}},' as "Tajima-Morosuke." Both texts identify this deity as a child of {{ill|Amenohiboko|fa|آمه‌نوهیبوکو|fr|Amenohiboko|id|Amenohiboko|ja|アメノヒボコ|ko|아메노히보코|zh|天日槍|qid=Q713100}} (Ame-no-Hihoko). The shrine name "Morosugi" is said to derive from "Morosuku (Morosuke)"{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}.

As noted above, the enshrined deity is regarded as the legitimate heir of Ame-no-Hiboko, the deity who opened up the Izushi area. Throughout the Izushi region, in addition to Morosugi Shrine, shrines of the Ame-no-Hiboko lineage are widely distributed, including {{ill|Izushi Shrine|fr|Izushi-jinja|ja|出石神社|ko|이즈시 신사|zh|出石神社|qid=Q3156511}} (Toyooka, Izushi-chō Miyauchi), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mi-Izushi Shrine}} (Toyooka, Izushi-chō Kirino), {{ill|Nakashima Shrine|ja|中嶋神社|qid=Q11364695}} (Toyooka, Miyake), and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sugi Shrine}} (Toyooka, Izushi-chō Araki){{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}.

=== History ===
The date of founding is unknown. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was originally located in Mizukami Village (present-day Toyooka, Izushi-chō Mizukami), near Izushi Shrine, and was transferred to its present location in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}){{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}. Since Tajima-Morosuku (Tajima-Morosuke), from whom the name "Morosugi" derives, appears in both the 'Kojiki' and 'Nihon Shoki' and is moreover identified as the legitimate heir of Ame-no-Hiboko, Morosugi Shrine is considered to have been established in ancient times{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}. The Mizukami area, said to be the shrine's original site, remains part of Morosugi Shrine's parishioner territory to this day, and during festivals a portable shrine procession (mikoshi togyo) is conducted all the way to Mizukami{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}{{Sfn|水上村（平凡社）|1999年}}.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is recorded as "Morosugi Shrine / Morosugi Shrine" under {{ill|Tajima Province|cs|Tadžima (provincie)|de|Provinz Tajima|es|Provincia de Tajima|fa|ولایت تاجیما|fr|Province de Tajima|gl|Provincia de Tajima|id|Provinsi Tajima|it|Tajima (provincia)|ja|但馬国|ko|다지마국|lt|Tadžimos žemė|nl|Tajima (provincie)|pt|Província de Tajima|ru|Тадзима (провинция)|simple|Tajima Province|sk|Tadžima (provincia)|sr|Провинција Таџима|tr|Tajima (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тадзіма|zh|但馬國|zh_min_nan|Tazima-kok|qid=Q1053727}} {{ill|Izushi District, Hyōgo|ja|出石郡|zh|出石郡|qid=Q11395767}}, and is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}.

Subsequent history is not well documented, but as mentioned above, in Tenshō 2 (1574), when the {{ill|Yamana clan|Q2975406|qid=Q2975406}} relocated from {{ill|Konosumiyama Castle|Q11545747|qid=Q11545747}} to {{ill|Arikoyama Castle|Q11516348|qid=Q11516348}}, Morosugi Shrine was also transferred from Mizukami Village to its present location below the castle{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was enshrined north of the yamato-no-kuruwa (mountain villa enclosure) of {{ill|Izushi Castle|de|Burg Izushi|es|Castillo Izushi|fa|قلعه ایزوشی|fr|Château d'Izushi|ja|出石城|zh|出石城|qid=Q2968296}}{{Sfn|内町（平凡社）|1999年}}, and received reverence from the successive castle lords of the {{ill|Koide clan (Negi Daibu)|Q11459112|qid=Q11459112}}, {{ill|Matsudaira clan|Q1141077|qid=Q1141077}}, and {{ill|Sengoku clan|Q11378184|qid=Q11378184}}, who provided for shrine construction and donations of offerings<ref name="説明板"/>. During the Sengoku clan's tenure as castle lords, it was customary for the lord himself to visit Morosugi Shrine upon returning from {{ill|Sankin-kōtai|Q1151844|qid=Q1151844}}{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}. During the Edo period, the shrine was also known as "Morosugi Daimyōjin"{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in October of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, and on April 21 of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 13 ({{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}}), it was elevated to {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}<ref name="説明板"/>. In the interim, the shrine buildings were destroyed by fire in Meiji 9 ({{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}}), but were rebuilt in Meiji 17 ({{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}})<ref name="説明板"/>.

=== Precinct ===
* Honden - Three bays on the front, two bays on the rear, and two bays on the sides, in {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} style, with a chidori-hafu (cusped gable) on the front. The roof is clad in copper sheeting<ref name="説明板"/>.
* Haiden - irimoya-zukuri style with a tiled roof{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}.
* Mikoshi storehouse

=== Festivals ===
* Annual festival (Sunday before October 15)
*: Formerly held on September 9, and later on October 15{{Sfn|諸杉神社（式内社）|1984年}}. Together with {{ill|Isobe Shrine (Toyooka)|Q11587232|qid=Q11587232|lt=Isobe Shrine}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ifukube Shrine}}, a "danjiri matsuri" is held in which approximately 20 {{ill|danjiri|Q11271630|qid=Q11271630}} are crashed into each other in front of Izushi Castle in a fighting festival.
